text: Every airliner in the sky right now is a metal balloon, pushing outward with tonnes of force.
At cruising height, the air is far too thin to breathe. So air is pumped into the cabin.
Inside, it feels like about eight thousand feet. And that air pushes on the skin, with more than five tonnes on every square metre.
So on every flight, the fuselage swells a tiny bit, then relaxes when it lands.
Thousands of flights later, that breathing can grow cracks. It's what tore apart the world's first jet airliner.
